title: Even moment bound by matching count
statement: Let $r,k,n$ be nonnegative integers with $n>0$, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube of dimension $n$ whose nonzero Fourier coefficients are all at level $k$. Then its $2r$-th moment under the uniform measure is at most the number of perfect matchings in the complete $2r$-partite graph with $k$ vertices in each part, divided by $(k!)^r$, and multiplied by the $r$-th power of the total Fourier weight at level $k$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is real-valued on the sign cube of dimension $n$
every nonzero Fourier coefficient of $f$ is at level $k$
